title: APT Design Lint Gates
source: Synchronized from apt-design-reference and canonical APT design doctrine
merge_policy: Critical failures block promotion unless an explicit decision record accepts the risk.
critical_gates: Brand identity is visible and consistent with the project profile.
Color usage is token-based and accessible.
Navigation, action, status, selection, focus, hover, and disabled states use the semantic color roles from design-tokens.json.
Primary calls to action, links, focus rings, selected navigation, and high-frequency action emphasis use the blue primary/action role.
The restricted accent is not the default hover, focus, CTA, or active navigation color; use it only for explicit support semantics such as badges, callouts, charts, and success treatment.
Raw color values, teal-as-default-CTA treatment, missing focus color, or ambiguous active navigation are critical failures unless a decision record accepts the exception.
Danger, warning, and success colors are used for semantic feedback only, not decoration.
Single-series charts lead with primary blue, multi-series charts use the approved chart ramp, and status colors appear only when they represent real status or risk.
Typography scale fits the surface and does not overflow containers.
Inter or the approved system fallback is used for UI/prose, and IBM Plex Mono is used for code, CLI examples, token values, prompts, and API examples.
Spacing and layout use stable responsive constraints.
Cards are used only for individual framed objects, not nested page structure.
Components use shared primitive families before inventing new interaction shapes.
Lucide-style outline icons and the AptEmblem pattern are used for interface iconography and APT brand marks where applicable.
Product chrome does not use emoji as decoration, status controls, navigation, headings, or action labels.
Motion is subtle, short, non-blocking, and respects reduced-motion expectations.
Loading, empty, success, error, disabled, permission, offline, and degraded states are defined where applicable.
Alerts, banners, toasts, badges, progress, skeletons, and status dots carry clear state meaning and do not rely on color alone.
Account, settings, and destructive flows include validation, recovery, confirmation, disabled states, and consent or terms handling where applicable.
Docs and content surfaces preserve source clarity, metadata, readable hierarchy, and anchor or table-of-contents behavior where useful.
Transactional email uses table-based layout, inline-safe styles, flattened token colors, a preheader, one primary call to action, and compliance or preference links where applicable.
Content is clear, specific, non-marketing, and aligned to APT naming and messaging rules.
Keyboard, focus, contrast, screen-reader, readable wrapping, and reduced-motion expectations are met.
AI-generated UI does not introduce unsupported styles, hidden behavior, invented components, or unreviewed visual language.
evidence_required: Primitive inventory covering navigation, controls, disclosure, feedback, and technical content
Token/component notes covering navigation, actions, status, selection, focus, hover, and disabled color roles
Chart semantics and color-role notes when data visualization is present
Surface-pattern notes for docs, content, product, account, dashboard, or email flows when applicable
Accessibility and contrast notes for primary, secondary, disabled, danger, warning, and success states
Keyboard, screen-reader, and reduced-motion notes for interactive surfaces
Vendored design-reference-kit path or equivalent preview evidence when a kit pattern is used
